record.question: A pharmacist is counselling an elderly patient who has hearing difficulty. The patient frequently asks for repetition. Which strategy best addresses this patient related physiological barrier.
options: Using visual aids to focus on the key concepts.
Skipping verbal counselling and only giving written instructions.
Providing instructions while facing away from the patient.
record.explanation: Answer B: Using visual aids to focus on the key concepts.. Visual aids can support communication for a patient with hearing difficulty; the pharmacist should also face the patient, speak clearly, and confirm understanding. Source/context note: The best real-world approach also includes facing the patient and using clear speech; these are absent from choices. Reference: https://www.nidcd.nih.gov/health/hearing-loss-older-adults. Verified worked solution, unofficial. Original printed wording and option order reviewed; no matching examiner key is asserted.
